correctness.rationale: The Alexander-dual faces have every four-set connected in C_n^3. The oriented 16-tetrahedron cross-polytope chain is a 3-cycle. For n>=14 the tetrahedron (0,2,4,7) has no possible 4-dimensional coface, making its signed characteristic cochain a genuine integral cocycle; the source supplies the exhaustive distance table. At n=13 a two-term wrapped cocycle cancels on the only five-simplex. Translated cycles and cocycles pair as the n-by-n integer identity (independently checked at n13,14,17), yielding a split regular Z[C_n] module, not just rational classes. At n12 the twelve-term signed cochain was evaluated on all 168 five-faces and pairs with the sphere cycle by a unit; direct mod2 ranks (161,152) and (207,130) give beta3 2,14. Integral Alexander duality shifts H^3 to H~_{n-6}; the sign twist of cyclic rotation leaves a regular representation isomorphic to itself. The infinite case rests on the written all-v vertex and cyclic gap arguments, not sampled n<=28.

originality.rationale: Bayer et al. and the 2026 Chauhan-Shukla paper establish general cut-complex definitions, hereditary shellability and k=3 shellability. A fully read Resultary cubic-PATH four-cut theorem plus heredity already implies mere nonshellability for sufficiently large cubic CYCLES; that weaker conclusion is explicitly excluded as original. Its single primitive Z path class does not give n linearly independent whole-cycle classes. A fully read published three-cut cycle-power rational character result concerns a different cut size, coefficient ring, degree and parameter range. No searched equivalent integral rank-n module for the 4-cut cubic CYCLE was found, subject to unindexed priority.
